out.subject: Bar stock offer – volume pricing and contract variants
out.body:
Dear Mr Aigner,

Thank you for your offer and the explanation of the alloy, labour and producer-price movements. Those movements deserve consideration, but the annual volume and a longer contract should also be reflected in your pricing.

For the proposed 24-month contract, our binding annual volume is 94800 kg. The attached forecast provides the monthly demand profile; please also see the figures below.

Please quote your dedicated volume-tier price for both variants side by side so we can compare them: EUR 4.58/kg fixed throughout the term, without an index clause; and EUR 4.44/kg with the AS-14404 clause, a 45% material share, no deadband and August 2026 as the base month. Both packages provide for 90 days net payment and a 24-month term, with DAP delivery.

Please distinguish the base price and alloy surcharge clearly in your reply and confirm the terms for each variant.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing
out.rationale: Open with the deepest available level for the fixed and indexed packages, keeping payment and duration identical. Provide the fixed annual volume and forecast, acknowledge the supplier's market explanation, and request comparable volume-tier quotations.

out.subject: Re: Bar supply – revised pricing for both variants
out.body:
Dear Mr Aigner,

Thank you for recognising the committed volume and confirming the 24-month term. Your explanation refers to standard payment terms, while your detailed offer includes 90 days net. We are proceeding on the basis of that 90-day variant; we are not requesting the shorter-payment option.

We understand your objection to a fully fixed price. The fixed-price alloy cover described in your letter nevertheless supports reconsidering that variant. Your own purchase-order history also provides a useful reference for this discussion; please see the figures below.

We can increase our proposal to EUR 4.77/kg fixed throughout the term without an index clause, or EUR 4.63/kg with your AS-14404 clause, a 45% material share, no deadband and August 2026 as the base month. Both remain on 90 days net and a 24-month contract, with DAP delivery.

Please review both variants side by side and show the base price and alloy surcharge separately. We do not need disclosure of your proprietary cost breakdown.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing
out.rationale: Increase both prices at the same level while preserving the two packages. Hold the detailed offer's payment terms, address the fixed-price objection using the supplier's stated alloy cover, and introduce its purchase-order history as fresh evidence.

out.subject: Re: Bar stock pricing – revised package proposals
out.body:
Dear Mr Aigner,

Thank you for reducing the indexed price and maintaining 90 days net and the 24-month term. I understand that your alloy cover does not extend over the full contract and that you therefore favour the indexed variant.

The recent movement in the producer-price series you cited also deserves consideration alongside the annual movement in your original offer. Please see the verified figures below and take these into account when reviewing the base price.

We can increase our proposal to EUR 4.77/kg with your AS-14404 clause, a 45% material share, no deadband and August 2026 as the base month. For the fixed-price comparison, our revised proposal is EUR 4.92/kg without an index clause. Both packages retain 90 days net, a 24-month term and DAP delivery.

Please review these revised prices, with particular attention to the indexed variant, and distinguish the base price from the alloy surcharge in your reply.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing
out.rationale: Raise both price proposals while retaining the existing payment and contract terms. Acknowledge the supplier's objection to full-term fixed pricing and prioritise its indexed variant, supported by the unused verified producer-price claim.
